title: T-426: YIELD-AT-NEXT wired into blackboard.py next (PR-062 consequence)
subject: reputation-phase-b-consumer
ratio: (1) THE PARAMETER. The operational parameter this record attaches a consequence to is CLAIM PRIORITY ORDERING (PR-061 clause 1; PR-060 clause 1's "which task is claimed, in what order"), settled operational under PR-060 as cured by RAT-01 by PR-061, and specified for next by PR-062 disposing case C-002. (2) THE CONSEQUENCE, YIELD-AT-NEXT, ATTACHED VERBATIM. blackboard.py next now yields its own recommendation -- not the recommended task, not claim -- when the requesting identity is outranked by another live candidate (an identity holding an unexpired claim): "outranked" means that candidate's Phase B total_score, read from the SAME dispatch --json call that already produced the advisory line, is STRICTLY GREATER than the requester's, zero margin. On a yield, next prints the identical "next:"/"claim it:" lines it always has, adds one line naming the outranking identity, logs one named event (phase_b_yield, carrying task/agent/outranked_by) to the blackboard's own events.jsonl, and returns PHASE_B_YIELD_EXIT (2) -- a code distinct from 0 (recommendation given) and 1 (no claimable task at all). Ties and identities unranked by dispatch never yield and fall back to today's (priority, id) order; a closed gate or any dispatch refusal keeps today's order with the printed reason and never yields; claim is untouched -- it stays first-come exactly as before. The two other alternatives D-002 considered, ADVISORY (print the order, bind nothing) and DEFER-AT-CLAIM (refuse claim itself for a bounded window), are NOT what this record attaches; YIELD-AT-NEXT is, verbatim, the Schulze winner PR-062 adopted. (3) THE ACT. This is T-426's own act of setting that parameter for the first time, at .harness/bin/blackboard.py:522-575 (cmd_next, phase_b_yield_check, PHASE_B_YIELD_EXIT): one subprocess read of reputation.py dispatch serves both the advisory line and the yield check -- never a second dispatch run, per PR-062 clause 4; no field is added to blackboard.json; no file reputation.py owns is written. The rename bypass PR-062 clause 5 names is documented, not hidden, in phase_b_yield_check's own docstring: identity is self-asserted (PR-023 clause 4), so a requester running next --agent <top identity> is never outranked, its payoff is nil because claim stays first-come, and the deviation is legible in events.jsonl without a verdict. (4) WHAT THIS RECORD DOES NOT DO. It sets no margin, threshold or window; reads no Phase A figure; binds no verb but next; and authorizes no second consequence -- PR-060 clause 6 requires its own published record for any further one.
scope_conditions: blackboard.py next only, gate open (VERIFIED, activation on); status, claim and every other verb are untouched. Applies only while PR-062 stands and while blackboard.py's dispatch seam (T-422) reads recommended_claim_order and candidates[].total_score from one reputation.py dispatch --json call per next invocation.
